messages.Albania: Albania remains deeply alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian suffering in Gaza and fully supports urgent action to protect civilians and secure the immediate, unconditional release of all hostages. However, to ensure a balanced, principled, and effective Council response, the text must unequivocally condemn the horrific terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October and reaffirm Israel's right to self-defence under international law. We urge the penholder to reflect these critical elements in the draft.
messages.China: China is a proud co-sponsor of this draft resolution and fully supports the text as presented. In the face of the unfolding humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, an immediate humanitarian ceasefire is the overwhelming call of the international community and the only viable path to save lives and restore peace. We urge the Security Council to heed the Secretary-General's urgent appeal under Article 99 and adopt this draft resolution without delay.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador is deeply alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian crisis unfolding in Gaza and supports the urgent call for a humanitarian ceasefire and the immediate release of all hostages. However, to enhance the text's balance and bolster its moral authority and consensus, the Council should explicitly condemn the 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas. We remain constructively engaged and prepared to support the resolution given the extreme gravity of the situation on the ground.
messages.France: France fully recognizes the catastrophic humanitarian emergency in Gaza and supports the urgent demand for a humanitarian ceasefire, unhindered aid delivery, and the unconditional release of all hostages. However, it is essential that the Security Council does not remain silent regarding the horrific terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October. We urge the penholder to include an explicit condemnation of these terrorist acts in order to reflect a balanced text capable of commanding the broadest possible support.
messages.Gabon: Gabon fully supports this draft resolution and the urgent demand for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire to save civilian lives and halt the catastrophic humanitarian crisis in Gaza. In the face of unprecedented human suffering, the Council cannot remain paralyzed and must act decisively in accordance with its mandate. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text as presented.
messages.Ghana: Ghana fully supports the draft resolution and welcomes its clear call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, full adherence to international humanitarian law, and the unconditional release of all hostages. The unsustainable civilian toll and rapidly deteriorating humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demand decisive and unified action from the Security Council. We encourage maximum consensus among members to ensure the Council can finally fulfill its primary responsibility to protect civilian lives.
messages.Japan: Japan shares the grave concern expressed by the Secretary-General regarding the catastrophic humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip and stresses the urgent need to protect civilians and secure the unconditional release of all hostages. In order to achieve the broadest possible consensus and reflect the realities on the ground, we believe the text should explicitly condemn the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas. Japan stands ready to engage constructively to enable the Council to act decisively to address the humanitarian crisis.
messages.Malta: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, Malta fully supports the text as drafted and urges its swift adoption without delay. Given the catastrophic humanitarian collapse in the Gaza Strip and the invocation of Article 99 by the Secretary-General, an immediate humanitarian ceasefire is urgently required to save civilian lives, protect children, enable humanitarian assistance at scale, and secure the unconditional release of all hostages. We urge all Council members to demonstrate collective responsibility and unite behind this critical text.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique fully supports the draft resolution as presented. In light of the catastrophic humanitarian crisis unfolding in the Gaza Strip and the unprecedented suffering of civilians, an immediate humanitarian ceasefire is urgently required. We stand ready to vote in favour of this text to protect civilian lives, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and secure the unconditional release of all hostages.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation fully supports this draft resolution and is proud to be among its co-sponsors. In light of the catastrophic humanitarian crisis unfolding in Gaza and the Secretary-General's invocation of Article 99, the Security Council must urgently fulfill its mandate and demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. We urge all members of the Council to vote in favour of this text as drafted, without attempts to weaken or delay it.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland fully supports the call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and the unconditional release of all hostages, given the catastrophic humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. To reflect a balanced approach, we strongly encourage the inclusion of an explicit condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas and recognition of applicable international law. We stand ready to support this vital humanitarian initiative to alleviate civilian suffering and ensure respect for international humanitarian law.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates fully supports this draft resolution as tabled and urges its swift adoption without delay or dilution. Following the Secretary-General's invocation of Article 99 and in light of the catastrophic humanitarian situation across the Gaza Strip, the Council must act decisively to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. We call on all Council members to unite behind this clear and necessary text to protect civilian lives and secure the unconditional release of all hostages.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support a text that remains silent on the atrocities committed by Hamas against innocent Israeli civilians on 7 October and ignores Israel's right to defend itself in line with international humanitarian law. A simple call for an immediate ceasefire risks freezing the conflict while Hamas continues to hold hostages, embed itself among civilians, and retain the capability to launch further attacks. We urge the penholders to include explicit condemnation of Hamas and focus the text on meaningful, extended humanitarian pauses.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support a draft resolution that calls for an unconditional ceasefire, which would leave Hamas in control of Gaza and able to repeat the atrocities of 7 October. It is unacceptable that the text completely fails to condemn Hamas's brutal terrorist attack or acknowledge Israel's right to defend its citizens. We urge the penholders to reflect the realities on the ground by supporting humanitarian pauses and demanding accountability from Hamas rather than advancing an unbalanced text.

steps.summary: In line with Brazil's established role as a pragmatic bridge-builder committed to international humanitarian law and Council effectiveness, the revised draft incorporates explicit condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas and reaffirms the right to self-defence under international law. To avert a veto while securing urgent relief on the ground, the operational mechanism has been aligned with urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors to enable immediate aid delivery and the unconditional release of all hostages. These balanced revisions preserve the core humanitarian imperative of protecting civilians while ensuring the draft commands the requisite support for adoption.
steps.text:
The Security Council,
Guided by the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,
Recalling all of its relevant resolutions on the situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question, in particular resolution 2712 (2023),
Unequivocally condemning the heinous terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas and other armed groups in Israel starting on 7 October 2023, including the taking and killing of hostages, murder, and sexual violence, as well as the ongoing rocket fire against Israeli civilians,
Reaffirming the inherent right of all States to individual and collective self-defence in accordance with Article 51 of the Charter of the United Nations and international law, including international humanitarian law,
Expressing grave concern over the catastrophic humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip and the suffering of the Palestinian civilian population,
Emphasizing that the Palestinian and Israeli civilian populations must be protected in accordance with international humanitarian law, and reaffirming the obligation of all parties to respect international humanitarian law and international human rights law,

1. Calls for urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors throughout the Gaza Strip to enable full, rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access and to facilitate the release of all hostages;
2. Reiterates its demand that all parties comply with their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law, notably with regard to the protection of civilians;
3. Demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, as well as ensuring humanitarian access;
4. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

before.Brazil:
Brazil has submitted this draft resolution out of a profound sense of responsibility and moral urgency in the face of the catastrophic humanitarian crisis unfolding before our eyes in the Gaza Strip.

The civilian population in Gaza is enduring unimaginable suffering, with essential infrastructure collapsed and access to food, water, fuel, and medical care critically compromised. The Security Council cannot remain paralyzed while human lives hang in the balance.

This draft resolution unequivocally condemns the heinous terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October, reiterates the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and reaffirms the obligation of all parties to strictly comply with international humanitarian law and protect civilians. At the same time, it urgently calls for extended humanitarian pauses and corridors to enable the rapid, unhindered delivery of lifesaving assistance across Gaza.

We urge all Council members to demonstrate unity and political will by voting in favour of this draft resolution, placing the preservation of human life and our collective obligations under the United Nations Charter above all else.
before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has consistently advocated for an immediate, durable, and fully observed humanitarian ceasefire as the only viable way to end the bloodshed and alleviate the catastrophic humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in the Gaza Strip. 

Unfortunately, the draft resolution before us once again falls short of this imperative. Instead of demanding a genuine cessation of hostilities, the text limits itself to calling for "humanitarian pauses." Experience has shown that temporary pauses cannot resolve the humanitarian catastrophe and will only lead to further escalation and suffering for Palestinian civilians once hostilities resume. Furthermore, the inclusion of language on Article 51 fails to reflect the reality that Israel, as the occupying power, cannot claim the right to self-defence under the UN Charter in that capacity, as affirmed by the International Court of Justice in its 2004 advisory opinion.

Because our principled amendments calling for an immediate ceasefire and removing the flawed reference to self-defence were not accommodated, the Russian Federation cannot support this draft. At the same time, mindful of the efforts of the penholder and the urgent humanitarian needs on the ground, we will not block it, and will therefore abstain.

after.Albania:
Mr. President,

Albania welcomes the adoption of this resolution and thanks Brazil for its tireless efforts, dedication, and leadership in bringing the Council together around a balanced and necessary text.

Albania voted in favour because this resolution responds directly to our principled and consistent position. It addresses the core priorities of this crisis with clarity and moral conviction. 

First, it unequivocally condemns the heinous terrorist attacks committed by Hamas and other armed groups on 7 October against Israel. Hamas is a terrorist organization; its barbaric acts cannot be justified under any circumstances, and they do not represent the legitimate aspirations of the Palestinian people. The resolution rightly demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Their safety and liberation must remain an urgent priority for the international community.

Second, the resolution explicitly reaffirms the inherent right of all States to self-defence under Article 51 of the Charter of the United Nations. Israel has the right and the duty to defend its people against terrorism, just like any other nation under attack, in strict compliance with international law and international humanitarian law.

At the same time, we cannot remain indifferent to the catastrophic humanitarian crisis unfolding in the Gaza Strip. The civilian population—particularly children, women, and the wounded—is enduring immense suffering. International humanitarian law is clear: civilians and civilian infrastructure, including hospitals and schools, must be protected at all times. The call for urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors is crucial to allow the rapid, safe, and unhindered delivery of lifesaving humanitarian assistance to all those in desperate need.

Today, the Security Council has demonstrated that it can overcome division and shoulder its responsibility for international peace and security. We must now ensure that this resolution is fully implemented on the ground, while continuing to work toward a lasting political solution based on the two-State solution, where Israelis and Palestinians can live side by side in peace, dignity, and security.

I thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution just adopted, which we also co-sponsored. 

For more than two months, the conflict in Gaza has caused an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe. Over 15,000 Palestinian civilians have lost their lives, a vast majority of them women and children, while millions are displaced and deprived of basic necessities, facing a complete breakdown of medical services and civil order. The conscience of humanity is being severely tested, and the Security Council cannot afford to be an onlooker.

China has consistently stood on the side of peace, justice, and humanity. Today’s adoption of this resolution represents an important step forward by the Security Council to alleviate the acute humanitarian crisis and protect civilian lives. We appreciate the tireless efforts of Brazil and other co-sponsors to forge consensus under difficult circumstances.

At the same time, we must recognize that temporary pauses alone cannot substitute for a lasting cessation of hostilities. Only an immediate, comprehensive, and durable ceasefire can truly halt the bloodshed, avert an even greater regional catastrophe, and give hope to civilians in Gaza and the hostages awaiting reunification with their families. We call on all parties to strictly comply with their obligations under international humanitarian law, immediately lift the siege on Gaza, protect civilians and civilian infrastructure—especially hospitals and humanitarian workers—and facilitate full, safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access.

Mr. President,

The recurring crises in the Middle East demonstrate once again that the Palestinian question remains the core of the issue. The historical injustice suffered by the Palestinian people cannot continue indefinitely. China will continue to work tirelessly with the international community to implement relevant Security Council resolutions, promote an immediate and lasting ceasefire, and push for a comprehensive, just, and lasting settlement through the two-State solution, so that the Palestinian and Israeli peoples may both live in peace and security.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Ecuador:
Mr. President,

Ecuador voted in favour of the resolution that has just been adopted, as it responds to the imperative need for the Security Council to act decisively in the face of the grave humanitarian crisis affecting the civilian population in the Gaza Strip.

My delegation welcomes the adoption of this text, which strikes a necessary balance. We reiterate our unequivocal condemnation of the terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October, as well as the taking of hostages. Nothing can justify acts of terrorism. We reiterate our demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and for humanitarian access to be granted to them without delay.

At the same time, we express our profound concern over the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the devastating loss of civilian lives, particularly women and children. International humanitarian law must be respected by all parties at all times, without exception. States have the legitimate right to defend their population and security, but this right must be exercised in strict accordance with international law, including the principles of distinction, precaution, and proportionality.

The establishment of urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors is indispensable to ensure the full, safe, rapid, and unhindered delivery of essential aid, including water, food, fuel, and medical supplies, and to allow for the evacuation of the wounded. 

This Council has a primary responsibility to maintain international peace and security. Today’s adoption demonstrates that, through constructive negotiation and political will, this body can overcome divisions and deliver meaningful tools to protect civilian lives and alleviate human suffering. Ecuador remains firmly committed to a peaceful, just, and lasting solution to the conflict, based on two democratic States living side by side within secure and recognized borders.

I thank you.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Brazil, and we welcome its adoption by the Security Council today.

Faced with the tragedy unfolding in the Middle East, it was high time for the Security Council to shoulder its responsibilities and speak with a clear and unified voice. 

First and foremost, this resolution unequivocally condemns the heinous terrorist attacks committed by Hamas and other terrorist groups against Israel and its people on 7 October. France reaffirms in the strongest terms its solidarity with Israel. We reiterate our demand for the immediate, unconditional, and complete release of all hostages still held in Gaza, among whom are French nationals.

Second, the text recalls the inherent right of Israel to defend itself. France has consistently stated that this right must be exercised in strict compliance with international law, and in particular international humanitarian law. The protection of civilian populations is an absolute, unconditional legal and moral imperative. Too many civilians have lost their lives in Gaza.

Third, the humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic. The Council's call for urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors is indispensable to ensure the full, rapid, safe, and unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid to all civilians in need, including food, water, fuel, and vital medical supplies, as well as to facilitate the evacuation of the wounded. These pauses must lead toward a lasting ceasefire.

Finally, we must not lose sight of the political horizon. Only a two-state solution, with two States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders, will bring just and lasting peace to the region. France remains fully committed to working with all partners to rebuild this political path.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Ghana:
Mr. President,

Ghana welcomes the adoption of today’s resolution and expresses its sincere appreciation to the delegation of Brazil and all co-sponsors for their tireless diplomatic efforts to bring the Security Council together around a common objective. 

From the outset of this crisis, Ghana has consistently maintained that the Security Council must speak with one voice to address the catastrophic situation unfolding in the Middle East. Today’s action demonstrates our collective resolve to prioritize the preservation of human life and to fulfill our primary responsibility under the Charter of the United Nations for the maintenance of international peace and security.

The humanitarian catastrophe in the Gaza Strip has reached unimaginable and unacceptable proportions. With essential services collapsed, hospitals crippled, and thousands of innocent civilians—especially children—bearing the brunt of the hostilities, urgent action is not merely a political necessity, but a profound moral imperative. 

Ghana voted in favour of this resolution because it addresses critical imperatives: demanding full compliance by all parties with their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law; establishing urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors to enable the rapid, safe, and unhindered delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance throughout Gaza; and demanding the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. 

We reiterate our condemnation of all acts of terrorism and violence against civilians, and we emphasize that international humanitarian law must be respected under all circumstances. Civilians and civilian infrastructure, including medical facilities and personnel, must be protected.

In conclusion, Mr. President, while the adoption of this resolution represents a vital step forward, our responsibility does not end with its passage. We urge all parties to faithfully implement its provisions without delay. Ultimately, lasting peace and security for both Israelis and Palestinians cannot be secured through force of arms, but only through a revived political process aimed at realizing the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders.

I thank you.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, and we welcome its adoption by the Council today. We express our deep appreciation to Brazil for its tireless leadership and constructive efforts to bridge differences among Council members to reach this crucial outcome.

The humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip is catastrophic, and the suffering of civilians, especially innocent children, has reached an unbearable level. Today, the Security Council has demonstrated that it can unite to address this humanitarian crisis.

Japan has consistently and unequivocally condemned the heinous terror attacks committed by Hamas and other armed groups on 7 October, which can never be justified under any circumstances. We reiterate our firm demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. 

At the same time, all parties must strictly abide by international law, including international humanitarian law. Japan reaffirms the right of all States to defend themselves and their citizens, but this right must be exercised in full compliance with international law. Civilians, humanitarian personnel, and medical facilities must be protected at all times. 

It is now paramount that this resolution be fully implemented on the ground. We call for the urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors to be realized without delay, so that life-saving humanitarian assistance—including water, food, fuel, and medical supplies—can reach all those in desperate need across the entire Gaza Strip in a safe, rapid, and unhindered manner. 

Japan will continue its proactive diplomatic engagements toward de-escalating the situation, improving the humanitarian conditions, and ultimately realizing a two-State solution where Israelis and Palestinians can live side by side in peace and security.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Malta:
Mr. President,

Malta voted in favour of the resolution just adopted and was proud to co-sponsor this text, submitted by Brazil. We welcome the Council’s adoption of this important resolution today, which demonstrates our collective responsibility to act when civilian lives and international peace and security hang in the balance.

The catastrophic humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip has reached unimaginable proportions. Thousands of innocent civilians, the vast majority of them women and children, have lost their lives. Essential infrastructure has collapsed, and hospitals and medical personnel are operating under impossible and harrowing conditions. The civilian population of Gaza cannot endure further deprivation of basic necessities, including food, water, fuel, electricity, and life-saving medical supplies.

This resolution builds upon resolution 2712 (2023), which this Council adopted last month under Malta's penholdership. By calling for urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors, this text reiterates our vital demand for full, rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access throughout the Gaza Strip to alleviate the immense suffering of civilians and facilitate rescue efforts.

At the same time, Malta reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of the heinous terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas across Israel on 7 October. We reaffirm our demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and for immediate humanitarian access to them. 

All parties to the conflict must strictly comply with their obligations under international law, in particular international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The principles of distinction, precaution, and proportionality are non-negotiable and must be respected at all times. Civilians, civilian infrastructure, and humanitarian and medical personnel must be protected.

Mr. President, while today’s adoption is a crucial and welcome step, words on paper must be translated into immediate action on the ground. We must also never lose sight of the political horizon. The only viable path to a just and enduring peace remains the two-State solution, based on the 1967 borders, where Israelis and Palestinians can live side by side in peace, dignity, and security.

Thank you.
after.Mozambique:
Mr. President,

Mozambique voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, and we would like to commend the delegation of Brazil for its tireless efforts, dedication, and leadership in steering this vital text to adoption.

Our vote reflects Mozambique’s profound and unwavering concern over the catastrophic humanitarian crisis unfolding in the Gaza Strip. The human cost of this conflict has reached unbearable levels, with thousands of innocent civilians—the vast majority of them women and children—losing their lives, while essential civilian infrastructure, including hospitals and medical facilities, has been severely crippled.

By supporting this resolution, Mozambique reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the protection of civilians and the scrupulous respect for international humanitarian law and international human rights law by all parties. The Security Council has sent a clear message: humanitarian pauses and corridors must be established urgently throughout Gaza to enable the rapid, safe, and unhindered delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance, including food, water, fuel, and medical supplies, to all those desperately in need. Furthermore, we reiterate our demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages.

The adoption of this text is a necessary step, but its true value lies in its full and immediate implementation on the ground. We call upon all parties to honour their obligations without delay.

Finally, Mr. President, while addressing the dire humanitarian emergency is paramount, we remain convinced that humanitarian measures alone cannot resolve this protracted crisis. Drawing from our own national experience, Mozambique firmly believes that lasting peace can only be attained through constructive dialogue and a viable political process. We reaffirm our commitment to a just, lasting, and comprehensive settlement through the two-State solution, where Israel and Palestine live side by side in peace and security, within internationally recognized borders.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Switzerland:
Mr. President,

Switzerland welcomes the adoption of this resolution and thanks Brazil and all the co-sponsors for their tireless efforts to find common ground within our Council. 

In the face of the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the continued suffering of civilians, united action by the Security Council is an imperative. Today’s decision sends a crucial signal of our collective responsibility.

Since 7 October, Switzerland has unequivocally condemned the heinous terrorist acts and rocket attacks perpetrated by Hamas against Israeli civilians, and we reiterate our demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. At the same time, we recognize Israel’s right to ensure its defence and security, which must be exercised in strict compliance with international law, in particular international humanitarian law.

The suffering of civilians in the Gaza Strip has reached intolerable levels. As the depositary of the Geneva Conventions, Switzerland recalls that international humanitarian law applies to all parties, at all times, without exception. The rules of distinction, proportionality, and precaution must be respected. Civilians, hospitals, medical personnel, and humanitarian facilities must be protected.

The urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors called for in this resolution must now be implemented without delay. Rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access throughout the Gaza Strip is essential to deliver lifesaving aid—food, water, fuel, and medical supplies—to the civilian population.

Finally, while addressing the immediate humanitarian catastrophe is vital, we cannot lose sight of the horizon beyond this crisis. Only a negotiated two-State solution, where Israelis and Palestinians live side by side in peace and security, can bring lasting peace and stability to the region. 

I thank you.
after.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President,

The United Arab Emirates voted in favour of the resolution adopted today, which we were proud to co-sponsor alongside Brazil and a broad coalition of Member States from across the globe. We thank Brazil for its leadership and tireless efforts to bring this Council together.

Our vote reflects our unwavering conviction that the Security Council could not remain silent or inactive while an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe continues to unfold in the Gaza Strip. More than 15,000 Palestinians have lost their lives, the vast majority of them women and children. Nearly the entire population of Gaza has been displaced, essential infrastructure has been decimated, and the health-care system has virtually collapsed. As we have said repeatedly in this chamber, there is no safe place in Gaza, and there is no hierarchy of civilian lives.

Today’s resolution represents an urgent and necessary step. By calling for extended humanitarian pauses and corridors throughout Gaza, the Council is demanding the space required to deliver life-saving assistance—food, water, fuel, and medical supplies—at scale to desperate civilians, to protect humanitarian workers, and to facilitate the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages.

At the same time, we must be clear-eyed: humanitarian pauses, while essential to alleviate immediate suffering and save lives, cannot be an end in themselves. The sheer scale of destruction and human despair demands nothing less than a full, durable humanitarian ceasefire. The Council cannot lose sight of that objective.

All parties must strictly comply with their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law. Civilians and civilian infrastructure, particularly hospitals and schools, must be protected at all times. Forced displacement must be unequivocally rejected.

Today, the Council demonstrated that it can act. But the true test of this resolution will not be its adoption; it will be its immediate and full implementation on the ground. The United Arab Emirates will continue to work tirelessly with regional and international partners to ensure aid reaches those in need, to end the hostilities, and to revive a credible political horizon toward a two-state solution where Palestinians and Israelis can live side by side in peace and security.

I thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President,

The United Kingdom voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. 

We welcome the Council’s ability today to speak with clarity and purpose on this grave crisis. For weeks, the United Kingdom has called for a balanced resolution that unequivocally addresses the core realities of the situation on the ground. Today, the Council has done so.

First, this resolution unequivocally condemns the heinous terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October, including murder, the taking of hostages, and acts of sexual violence. It rightly demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages still held in Gaza. Hamas’s brutality must never be repeated, and those abducted must be reunited with their families without delay.

Second, the resolution explicitly reaffirms the inherent right of all States to self-defence, in accordance with Article 51 of the UN Charter and international humanitarian law. Israel has the right to defend its people against Hamas and ensure that such atrocities cannot happen again.

At the same time, we remain deeply alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. The civilian population is enduring immense suffering. This resolution rightly calls for urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors to allow vital aid—food, water, fuel, and medical supplies—to enter Gaza at scale and reach those who need it most. 

All parties must strictly comply with international humanitarian law. Civilians must be protected, and hospitals and UN facilities must be safeguarded. 

Today’s resolution is an important step forward. We now urge its full and immediate implementation, and we will continue to work closely with international partners to alleviate civilian suffering, secure the release of all hostages, and pursue a credible pathway toward a lasting and sustainable peace based on a two-state solution.

Thank you, Mr President.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Today, the Security Council has finally spoken with clarity and purpose. The United States voted in favour of this resolution because it reflects the essential principles that must guide this Council’s response to the crisis in the Middle East.

First and foremost, this resolution unequivocally condemns the horrific terrorist attacks committed by Hamas and other groups against Israel on October 7—attacks that involved the murder, torture, and abduction of innocent men, women, and children, as well as appalling acts of sexual violence. For weeks, the Council failed to name Hamas or condemn its atrocities. Today’s resolution rights that wrong.

Second, the resolution explicitly reaffirms the inherent right of all States to self-defence under Article 51 of the Charter of the United Nations. Israel has both the right and the responsibility to defend its citizens from terrorism and to ensure that the horrors of October 7 can never be repeated. At the same time, as we have consistently made clear at the highest levels of our Government, how Israel defends itself matters. Democracies are distinguished by their adherence to international law, including international humanitarian law, and all feasible precautions must be taken to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure.

Third, this resolution demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages being held by Hamas and other terrorist organizations in Gaza. The families of these hostages have endured unspeakable agony for more than two months, and their safe return remains an urgent priority for President Biden and this administration.

Finally, we share the deep and agonizing concern over the humanitarian catastrophe facing Palestinian civilians in Gaza. Innocent lives are being lost, and the suffering is immense. That is why the United States has led intensive diplomatic efforts alongside partners in the region, including Egypt and Qatar, to secure humanitarian pauses that facilitate the delivery of critical food, water, medicine, and fuel, as well as the release of hostages. This resolution rightly calls for urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors, which offer a practical and realistic mechanism to surge life-saving aid to those in desperate need without leaving Hamas in control and free to rearm and repeat its attacks.

Mr. President, lasting peace cannot be built on slogans that ignore the realities on the ground. Today, the Council came together to adopt a balanced, actionable resolution that condemns terror, supports the protection of innocent civilians, and demands the release of all hostages. The United States will continue to work tirelessly with our partners across the region and around this table to implement these commitments and to lay the groundwork for a durable peace where Israelis and Palestinians can live side by side with equal measures of security, freedom, and dignity.

Thank you.
